a1.say: Let's solve The Link That Makes a Loop, using the Union-Find approach.

card.title: The Link That Makes a Loop

a1.cap: A tree of n nodes (labelled 1..n) got one extra edge, creating exactly one cycle. edges lists all edges. Return the edge that can be removed to make it a tree again; if several work, return the one that appears last.

lines: A tree of n nodes (labelled 1..n) got one extra edge, creating exactly one cycle. edges lists all edges. Return the edge that can be removed to make it a tree again; if several work, return the one that appears last.

a1.cap: For example, with edges = [[1,2],[1,3],[2,3]], the answer is [2,3].
a1.say: For example, with edges equals 1, 2, 1, 3, 2, 3, the answer is 2, 3.

a1.cap: Union-find tracks which nodes are already connected. Add edges in order: if both ends already share a root, this edge closes the cycle, so it's the answer. Otherwise merge their groups.
Let's walk through it with edges = [[1,2],[1,3],[2,3]].
a1.say: Let's walk through it with edges equals 1, 2, 1, 3, 2, 3.

a1.cap: Node 1 belongs to group 1, node 2 to group 2.
Node 1 belongs to group 2, node 3 to group 3.
Node 2 belongs to group 3, node 3 to group 3.
They're already connected, so [2, 3] closes the loop.
a1.say: They're already connected, so 2, 3 closes the loop.

a1.cap: Time complexity is O(n · α(n)) and extra space is O(n). With path compression each find is nearly constant time.
a1.say: Time complexity is O of n times alpha (n) and extra space is O of n. With path compression each find is nearly constant time.

a1.cap: That's the Union-Find approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
